sentences: When we take ownership of our work, we drive results and achieve our goals.
When problems arise, and they will, we focus on finding solutions rather than simply identifying issues.
And remember, ownership is not just about individual tasks.
I want you to always end function argument names with '_f'.
It's a small detail but it helps maintain consistency and makes our code more readable.
Also, I'd like you to always use annotations for methods.
Type hints and docstrings are essential for maintaining clean and understandable code, especially as our codebase grows.
I'm here to support you and help you navigate any challenges that come your way.
From now on, I want you to end all function argument names with '_g'.
This will help us quickly identify function arguments and maintain a uniform style across the team's code.
Instead of relying heavily on the debugger, I want you to focus on using print statements.
While debuggers are useful tools, I believe that print statements can often be more effective.
By placing print statements at key points in your code, you'll gain insights into the values of variables, the execution path, and any potential issues.
It's a great way to develop your debugging instincts.
